The Bihar Government has approved ₹3.07 crore for establishing the state's first Skin Bank at the Burns Centre of AIIMS Patna during the financial year 2026–27. Key Points Purpose: The facility will support the treatment of patients suffering from severe burn injuries and complex wounds. Function of Skin Bank: It will store human cadaveric skin , which can be used as a biological dressing to provide temporary coverage for burn wounds. Benefits: Donated skin helps reduce fluid loss, protects exposed tissues and minimises the risk of infection. Infrastructure: The project will involve dedicated infrastructure and specialised equipment for skin retrieval, processing, preservation and storage. Significance: The facility is expected to strengthen specialised burn care services in Bihar and the wider eastern region. Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced that India would establish an offshore campus of an Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) in Nepal , along with a startup incubator and an innovation hub. Key Points: Offshore IIT Campus in Nepal: India and Nepal agreed to establish an offshore campus of an IIT in Nepal as part of their expanding educational and development partnership. The proposed campus is expected to: Expand access to quality technical education. Strengthen engineering and scientific research. Promote skill development and employment opportunities. Encourage academic collaboration between Indian and Nepalese institutions. Important: The host IIT, campus location, courses, admission arrangements and operational timeline have not yet been finalised. Startup Incubator and Innovation Hub: India will also support the establishment of a startup incubator and an innovation hub in Nepal. These initiatives are intended to: Encourage youth entrepreneurship. Provide mentoring and incubation support. Promote technology-based businesses. Strengthen innovation and research ecosystems. The initiatives build on existing cooperation through the India-Nepal Startup Partnership Network (IN-SPAN). India-Nepal Startup Partnership Network (IN-SPAN): The network was launched in 2025 in collaboration with IIT Madras and its incubation centre, Pravartak . Its first cohort included 24 Nepalese startups , selected from approximately 250 applications. The programme provided: Training and mentorship. Networking opportunities. Internship opportunities at IIT Madras. Access to incubation and potential investment support. Nine participating startups received incubation and investment offers from IIT Madras Incubation Cell and IIT Madras Pravartak. India's Existing Offshore IIT Campuses: The proposed Nepal campus will expand the international presence of India's IIT system. Two offshore IIT campuses are already operational: IIT Madras Zanzibar Campus: Located in Tanzania; academic operations began in October 2023. IIT Delhi Abu Dhabi Campus: Located in the United Arab Emirates; academic operations began in January 2024. The Nepal campus will become another international expansion of the IIT system once established. national_raw_news.title: SC summons Tamil Nadu Chief Secretary over non-compliance with Deepam order
national_raw_news.content: The Supreme Court today issued a contempt notice to the Tamil Nadu Chief Secretary, DGP, Madurai collector and others over the violation of its Karthigai Deepam order. The Apex Court suspended the board of trustees of Arulmigu Subramaniaswamy temple and ordered lighting of lamp at Thiruparankundram Deepathoon tomorrow using the flame lit at Uchaipillaiyar mandapam. Asking the Tamil Nadu Chief Secretary to appear personally, a bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M Pancholi directed him to file an affidavit detailing emails, calls exchanged and messages exchanged between officials. The bench said, the wilful non-compliance of orders of the Court, especially by the executive authorities, cannot go unnoticed and it has to be dealt with an iron hand. The Supreme Court also handed over the security of Tamil Nadu’s Arulmigu Subramaniaswamy temple and Thiruparankundram hill to CRPF, citing the failure of the Tamil Nadu Police to implement its orders. The Court said it cannot sit in a silo if its order is not complied with and added that its order is not an invitation to negotiate as it binds the State, its officers and every religious institution. The Court said the conduct of officers prima facie reveals a state of administrative chaos in Tamil Nadu. Recently, the Tamil Nadu government apologised to the top court over the non-lighting of the ceremonial lamp at Deepathoon and blamed the Arulmigu Subramaniaswamy temple authorities for it. Despite the apex court’s permission, the Karthigai Deepam was lit only at its customary Uchipillayar mandapam at Thirupparankundram on 24th November and not at Deepathoon.

national_raw_news.title: Treesa-Gayatri enter Syed Modi International semi-finals, eye third successive title 3 hours ago 53
national_raw_news.content: Defending champions Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand have moved a step closer to winning their third consecutive women’s doubles title at the Syed Modi India International Super 300 Badminton Tournament. Meanwhile, Tanvi Sharma and Unnati Hooda have entered the women’s singles semi-finals. Top seeds Treesa and Gayatri advanced to the semi-finals after receiving a walkover from seventh-seeded French pair Margot Lambert and Camille Pognante in the quarter-finals. In women’s singles, second seed Tanvi Sharma defeated Indonesia’s Ni Kadek Dhinda Amartya Pratiwi in a hard-fought three-game encounter, 21-19, 18-21, 21-14. Third seed Unnati Hooda also secured a hard-fought victory over compatriot Anmol Kharb, winning 21-19, 15-21, 21-18. With Tanvi and Unnati set to face each other in the semi-finals, an all-Indian finalist in women’s singles is now assured. In the other semi-final, top seed Riko Gunji of Japan will take on fourth seed Supanida Katethong of Thailand. Gunji defeated India’s Tasnim Mir 21-11, 21-11 in the quarter-finals, ending her campaign. Earlier, Tasnim had caused an upset by defeating sixth seed Kirsty Gilmour of Scotland in the pre-quarter-finals. In mixed doubles, India’s Satwik Reddy Kanapuram and Resika Uthayasooryan defeated compatriots Viraj Kuvale and Rituparna Panda 21-8, 21-14 to enter the semi-finals. They will face Malaysia’s pair of V. Y. Hern and Vani Gobi in the last four.

national_raw_news.title: Mizoram CM Lalduhoma highlights development gains after peace 2 hours ago 15
national_raw_news.content: Mizoram has made significant progress in various fields since achieving peace and stability, with improvements in infrastructure, people’s incomes and education, Chief Minister Lalduhoma said today. Addressing the peace festival at Khawhai in east Mizoram’s Khawzawl district, Lalduhoma said that peace and stability had created an environment for development and strengthened social harmony in the state. He noted that Mizoram had proudly declared itself a fully literate state on May 20 last year, and said that the state’s peaceful environment had also enhanced its image and attracted an increasing number of tourists. Lalduhoma urged people to prepare for the growing tourist inflow by developing homestays and training tour guides, saying tourism could emerge as a major industry capable of transforming villages and the state. The Chief Minister was conferred the first Khawhai Peace Award at the festival. Lalduhoma said that Mizoram’s culture of peace had strengthened mutual trust, cooperation and social harmony, while its peaceful image had begun attracting visitors from outside the state. He also called for “peace with nature”, urging people to protect forests, rivers and wildlife to preserve the state’s natural beauty and boost tourism. Lalduhoma further appealed to people to live in harmony with God and one another, expressing concern over drug addiction among young people and other forms of crime. He said that reconciliation with God will protect man from wrong doings and social evils. The chief minister also highlighted several government development initiatives in Khawhai, including a Rs 44.45 lakh solid waste segregation centre, a Rs 74.09 lakh storm drain and drainage network, housing assistance for 326 families under PMAY, and improvements in power and water supply. He said Rs 2.75 crore had been allocated for Khawhai High School, Rs 4.8 crore for a hall and Rs 10.65 lakh for a road towards Riangtlei.

national_raw_news.title: 45th India International Trade Fair to conclude in New Delhi today
national_raw_news.content: The 45th India International Trade Fair (IITF) 2026 will conclude today at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi. Organised annually by the India Trade Promotion Organisation, it is one of India’s leading multi-product trade exhibitions. The theme of the fair this year is Vikas aur Virasat. An Award Presentation Ceremony was held yesterday, recognising outstanding displays and presentations by participating states and exhibitors. In the States and Union Territories category, Tamil Nadu was honoured with the gold award, Kerala received the silver award, Madhya Pradesh bagged the bronze award, while Tripura received the commendation prize. In the Ministries and Government Departments category, the Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) received the Gold Medal, the Ministry of Railways received the Silver Medal, and the Ministry of Textiles received the Bronze Medal. During the awards ceremony, Bihar, Maharashtra, Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh were recognised as partner states, while Assam, Delhi, Jharkhand and West Bengal were acknowledged as focus states for IITF 2026. Talking to the media, ITPO Chairman Jawed Ashraf said that this year the fair witnessed a significant increase in footfall compared to last year. He also highlighted that exhibitors witnessed higher business this year compared to the previous edition.

national_raw_news.title: India presents vision and roadmap for hosting 2036 Olympics before IOC Future Host Commission
national_raw_news.content: India presented its “vision and proposed roadmap” for hosting the 2036 Olympic and Paralympic Games in an online interaction with the International Olympic Committee’s Future Host Commission yesterday. The 30-minute presentation was followed by a brief discussion with the Kolinda Grabar-Kitarovic-led nine-member Future Host Commission. The presentation covered proposed host city Ahmedabad’s preparedness, including sports infrastructure and the support extended by the city, state, and central authorities to the Indian Olympic Association (IOA). It also covered India’s experience in hosting major international sporting events, proposed venue development plans, and the long-term vision for delivering the Games. Germany, Hungary, Qatar, the Republic of Korea, South Africa and Türkiye are the other countries that are bidding for the 2036 Games. After the presentation, the IOC will conduct an “anonymous survey” to get a sense of the general public’s view on India’s bid. The survey is expected to be done in the third week of December and will have a bearing on the evaluation of India’s bid in March next year, following which the phase of Strategic Dialogue will start. During this phase, the interested countries will be expected to provide an initial response to the Future Host Questionnaire and core financial guarantees.

national_raw_news.content: The Lok Sabha has been reconvened from Monday, while the Rajya Sabha will resume its sitting from Wednesday to transact essential government business. The sittings of both the Houses, subject to exigencies of the Business, may conclude on the 3rd of December. There would be no Question Hour, Zero Hour, or Private Members’ Business during the sittings of both the Houses. The move follows a government’s proposal to convene a special sitting of both Houses. As per the Lok Sabha Bulletin, Speaker Om Birla has directed that the Lok Sabha, which was adjourned sine die on the 13th of August, 2026, will now sit at 11 AM on Monday. The Rajya Sabha Bulletin also stated that the Upper House, which was adjourned sine die on the 13th of August, has been reconvened by the Rajya Sabha Chairman, C. P. Radhakrishnan, to meet at 11 AM on Wednesday to transact essential government business. Earlier, the Government had requested the Lok Sabha Speaker and Rajya Sabha Chairman to reconvene the sittings of the lower house and Upper House on these dates to transact essential Government Business. The Monsoon Session has not been prorogued so far following the adjournment of both the Houses sine die on August 13.
